tagline: Down the Maumee from Defiance, with the old canal alongside.
intro: From Defiance the byway follows the Maumee downstream through Napoleon, Grand Rapids and Waterville toward Maumee and Perrysburg, on a river that meanders northeast through farm country to Lake Erie. The Miami and Erie Canal ran alongside. It thrived for about thirty years before the railroads took its trade, and a flood in 1913 destroyed much of what was left.

Grand Rapids was still called Gilead in 1845, when the state built a large dam across the river there to keep the canals in water. It cut the water power of the village mill, and the citizens destroyed it.

moments.title: Independence Dam State Park
moments.text: Three miles east of Defiance the park's main entrance crosses the ruins of Lock 13, and seven preserved miles of the canal run on from here.

moments.title: Providence Metropark
moments.text: Lock 44 here is the only original working canal lock in Ohio, and the park's Ludwig mill of 1866 began as a sawmill and took to grinding grain in the 1880s.

moments.title: Fort Meigs
moments.text: Raised in 1813 on the south bank, it was the largest wooden-walled fort in North America, and that winter a sentry froze to death during his two hours on guard.
